title: Adrian of Utrecht (Cardinal of Tortosa) to Charles V, Valladolid, 9 September 1520: the cipher paragraph Danvila could not translate, read

steps.what: Key K1 from cipher/plain pairs of 8 Oct and 17 Nov 1520 (Bergenroth).
K1 on held-out 2,1,30: 0.636 of characters vs 200 controls max 0.212.
K3 on held-out 2,1,68 (frozen before 2,1,69 was opened): 0.851 of characters vs 200 controls max 0.216, but 0.541 of words; first version withdrawn on 28 Oct.
K4 on held-out 2,1,85 vs its contemporary transcription 2,1,83: 0.783 of characters (controls max 0.200).
K6 on held-out 2,1,88 vs Danvila (30 Aug 1521): 0.813 of characters (controls max 0.211).
Key K7: K6 rebuilt with 2,1,88 in training and sign shapes re-read blind by Brice Dudout on plates.

K7, one measurement on the fresh pair 2,1,99 (2nd cipher passage, 10 lines frozen) vs Danvila MHE XXXVIII (5 Dec 1521): 0.882 of characters (n = 170) vs 200 controls max 0.176, rank 1/201; words 0.770.

Daniel's lead of 7 Nov: fol. 434 of PTR,LEG,2,1,100 (cipher original of the paragraphs of 24 Oct 1521) transcribed by shape and frozen, decoded with frozen K7, then compared with Danvila's printed decipherment (MHE XXXVIII pp. 547-549): K7 reads it almost word for word. Existing pair, so used for training, not validation: derived key K7b (K7 + 18 entries, declared, not re-validated) gives three more words of 2,1,19 (quiça, quitar, villas).

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from cipher/plain pairs of the Cardinal's other letters of 1520-21 (sign shapes re-read blind on plates); key K7 validated by a single measurement on a fresh held-out pair (2,1,99 vs Danvila).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule, strict count (restored words not read): 46 cipher words, 28 certain, 15 probable, 2 restored (tales, vuestra), 1 unresolved (group fud.); 43 of 46 = 93.5% (97.8% with the restored words). Recount of 9 Nov 2026 after fol. 434 (key K7b): the first word {quiça} and {villas} are read, [juntar] is replaced by {quitar}. Earlier values: 0.87 (5 Nov, 40 of 46), 0.957.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): key K7 frozen, then one measurement on a fresh pair named before download, AGS PTR,LEG,2,1,99 (2nd cipher passage, 10 lines frozen) against Danvila's printed plain text (MHE XXXVIII, 5 Dec 1521): 0.882 of characters (n = 170) against max 0.176 for 200 shuffled-key controls (median 0.041), rank 1/201; words 0.770 (controls max 0.119). Criterion fixed in advance: characters >= 0.85 and >= best control + 0.30. Earlier keys: K3 0.851 chars / 0.541 words on 2,1,68 (withdrawn), K4 0.783 on 2,1,85, K6 0.813 on 2,1,88 (failed).

texts.label: Adrian of Utrecht to Charles V, Valladolid, 9 September 1520 (AGS PTR,LEG,2,1,19), cipher paragraph
texts.summary: On 9 September 1520 Adrian of Utrecht – Cardinal of Tortosa, regent of Castile for Charles V, and sixteen months later Pope Adrian VI – wrote from Valladolid while the Junta of the Comunidades was settling at Ávila. In the middle of the letter are six lines in cipher. Danvila, who printed the letter in 1897, noted only: “Sigue un párrafo cifrado que no ha podido traducirse”. The cipher is the Cardinal’s dotted code; we rebuilt it from his other letters of 1520–1521 whose plain text is known, validated it on a letter held out, and applied it to this paragraph. It tells what the Junta meant to do to the grandees: take from them the alcabalas and the towns that had belonged to the Crown.

reading_review.note: Re-read as sentences 9 Nov 2026 with the derived key K7b (fol. 434, not re-validated): 43 of 46 words read (28 certain, 15 probable, 2 restored, 1 unresolved: fud.), so grade B. First reading 2 Nov 2026. Key K7 validated 2 Nov 2026 by one measurement on a fresh held-out pair (AGS PTR,LEG,2,1,99, 2nd cipher passage, vs Danvila MHE XXXVIII, 5 Dec 1521): characters 0.882 vs at best 0.176 for 200 shuffled keys (rank 1/201); words 0.770. Sign shapes re-read blind by Brice Dudout on plates.

prior.where: Danvila MHE XXXVI p. 18 ("no ha podido traducirse"); Bergenroth 1868; repository; Cryptiana (28 Oct 2026).

human: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
